Remote Work Policy

Northstar Digital Services, Inc.
Enterprise Technology Office

Document ID: POL-HR-015 | Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 2026-01-01 | Classification: Internal

Field Value

Company Northstar Digital Services, Inc.

Document Owner Human Resources and Information Security

Audience Employees, contractors, managers, IT support, security, and finance teams

Purpose Sample enterprise content for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation demo
knowledge base

Review Cycle Annual or upon major business, security, compliance, or system change

1. Purpose

This policy defines remote and hybrid work expectations for Northstar Digital Services, Inc.. It supports employee
flexibility while protecting company data, systems, customers, and productivity.

2. Scope

• Applies to employees, contractors, interns, and temporary workers approved for remote or hybrid work.

• Applies to work performed from home offices, coworking spaces, hotels, client sites, and other non-company
locations.

• Applies to company-owned devices and approved bring-your-own-device exceptions.

3. Eligibility and Approval

Remote work eligibility is based on role requirements, manager approval, performance expectations, legal
requirements, and security considerations. Managers may modify or revoke remote work approval when
business, compliance, or performance needs require it.

4. Security Requirements

• Use company-approved devices for company work unless a documented exception is approved.

• Use MFA for all corporate systems.

• Connect through approved VPN, zero trust access, or managed access gateway when required.

• Do not store company confidential data on personal devices, personal cloud drives, or removable media.

• Lock screens when away and prevent family members, visitors, or unauthorized persons from viewing
company information.

• Report lost or stolen devices immediately to the Service Desk and Information Security.



Northstar Digital Services, Inc. | Internal Use Only Page 2

5. Work Environment Expectations

• Maintain a workspace suitable for confidential conversations and reliable work.

• Use a secure internet connection and avoid untrusted public Wi-Fi unless protected by approved secure
access controls.

• Be available during agreed working hours and attend required meetings.

• Follow all timekeeping, overtime, and attendance requirements applicable to the role and location.

6. Equipment and Support

Company equipment remains company property and must be returned upon request or at separation. IT support
is available for company-managed devices, standard software, and approved connectivity issues. Employees are
responsible for maintaining a safe workspace and reasonable internet reliability.

7. Data Handling

Data Type Remote Work Requirement

Public May be used in normal work channels.

Internal Use approved collaboration tools and access controls.

Confidential Store only in approved repositories; do not print unless business-approved.

Restricted Access only from managed devices and approved networks; follow
system-specific controls.

8. Policy Violations

Violations may result in removal of remote work privileges, access suspension, disciplinary action, contract
termination, or legal action depending on severity.

Field Value

Company Northstar Digital Services, Inc.

Document Owner Human Resources and Enterprise Technology Office

Audience Employees, contractors, managers, IT support, security, and finance teams

Purpose Sample enterprise content for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation demo
knowledge base

Review Cycle Annual or upon major business, security, compliance, or system change

1. Purpose

This policy defines the standard employee and contractor onboarding process for Northstar Digital Services, Inc..
The goal is to provide a consistent, secure, and auditable onboarding experience from offer acceptance through
the first 30 days of work.

2. Scope

• Applies to all full-time employees, part-time employees, interns, temporary workers, and contractors.

• Applies to corporate, remote, hybrid, and field-based workers.

• Covers HR setup, identity creation, equipment provisioning, application access, security training, and
manager responsibilities.

3. Roles and Responsibilities

Role Responsibilities

Hiring Manager Submit onboarding request, approve access, assign buddy, define first-week
goals.

Human Resources Confirm employment status, collect required documentation, schedule
orientation.

IT Service Desk Provision hardware, email, MFA, collaboration tools, and standard applications.

Information Security Validate least-privilege access, confirm training completion, monitor
exceptions.

New Hire Complete onboarding tasks, security training, policy acknowledgements, and
MFA enrollment.



Northstar Digital Services, Inc. | Internal Use Only Page 2

4. Onboarding Timeline

Timing Required Activities

T-10 to T-5 business
days

HR creates worker record; manager submits access request; IT prepares
laptop and account profile.

T-4 to T-1 business days Identity account created; MFA enrollment link issued; equipment shipped or
staged.

Day 1 Orientation, password setup, MFA setup, acceptable use acknowledgement,
security awareness assignment.

Days 2-5 Role-specific application access, team onboarding, knowledge base review,
project overview.

Days 6-30 Manager check-ins, completion audit, access validation, and removal of
unused temporary access.

5. Access Standards

• Access must be role-based and approved by the hiring manager or system owner.

• Administrative access is prohibited unless explicitly approved by Information Security.

• Temporary elevated access must include an expiration date not longer than 30 days.

• Shared accounts are not permitted unless approved by Information Security for a documented operational
reason.

6. Required Training and Acknowledgements

• Acceptable Use Policy

• Information Security Awareness Training

• Data Handling and Confidentiality Training

• Remote Work Policy acknowledgement when applicable

• Cloud Cost Policy acknowledgement for engineering, DevOps, data, and product teams

7. Exceptions

Exceptions require written approval from the hiring manager, HR, IT, and Information Security. Exceptions must
include a business justification, compensating controls, and an expiration date.

8. Compliance and Audit Evidence

The onboarding ticket, access approvals, equipment assignment, policy acknowledgements, and training
completion record must be retained for at least three years or longer if required by contract or regulation.

value.chunk: Password Reset GuideCompany: Northstar Digital Services, Inc.  Document Owner: IT Service Desk  Document ID: GUIDE-IT-020  Version: 1.0  Effective Date: 2026-01-01  Classification: Internal1. PurposeThis guide explains how employees and contractors reset their corporate password and recover access to Northstar Digital Services, Inc. systems. It is intended for standard user account recovery and does not apply to privileged administrator accounts, service accounts, or emergency security lockouts.2. When to Use This GuideUse this guide when:You forgot your password.Your password expired.You received a prompt to change your password.You can sign in but want to change your password proactively.The Service Desk asked you to complete a self-service password reset.Do not use this guide if you suspect your account was compromised. Instead, contact the IT Service Desk immediately and report a potential security incident.3. Password RequirementsPasswords must meet the following standards:Minimum length: 14 characters.Must not contain your name, username, company name, or common dictionary phrases.Must be unique and not reused from other personal or business accounts.Must not be shared with coworkers, managers, vendors, family members, or IT support.Must be changed immediately if you believe it has been exposed.A passphrase such as `BlueRiver!TrainWindow92` is easier to remember and stronger than a short complex password.4. Self-Service Password Reset StepsGo to the company sign-in page from a trusted browser.Select Forgot password or Can’t access your account.Enter your company email address.Complete multi-factor authentication using your enrolled method.Choose a new password that meets the password requirements.Confirm the new password.Sign out of all active sessions when prompted.Sign back in using the new password.5. After Resetting Your PasswordAfter your password is changed, update any signed-in company applications on your laptop, phone, or tablet. Common applications include:Email and calendar.VPN or secure access client.Collaboration tools.Password manager.Developer tools and command-line credentials.Mobile device mail profile, if approved for company use.6. Multi-Factor Authentication IssuesIf you cannot complete MFA:Confirm that your phone has internet or cellular service.Try an alternate enrolled MFA method, if available.Check whether your authenticator app time sync is enabled.Contact the IT Service Desk if your device was replaced, lost, stolen, or reset.The Service Desk will verify your identity before changing MFA methods.7. Locked AccountsYour account may lock temporarily after too many failed sign-in attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again, or contact the IT Service Desk if the issue continues. Repeated lockouts may indicate a saved old password on another device or application.8. Security RemindersIT will never ask you to disclose your password.Do not approve MFA prompts you did not initiate.Report suspicious password reset emails, unexpected MFA prompts, or unusual account activity.Use the company-approved password manager for work credentials.Do not store passwords in notes, spreadsheets, browsers without approval, or chat messages.9. Service Desk EscalationContact the IT Service Desk when:Self-service reset fails.You lost access to all MFA methods.You suspect account compromise.Your account is locked repeatedly.A privileged or service account password needs to be changed.When contacting support, provide your name, department, callback number, device type, and a brief description of the issue. Do not include your current or previous password.10. Audit and CompliancePassword reset events, MFA changes, and Service Desk identity verification records may be logged for security, compliance, and audit purposes. Logs are retained according to the company retention schedule.

Enterprise Technology Office

Document ID: POL-FIN-204 | Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 2026-01-01 | Classification: Internal

Field Value

Company Northstar Digital Services, Inc.

Document Owner Cloud Center of Excellence

Audience Employees, contractors, managers, IT support, security, and finance teams

Purpose Sample enterprise content for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation demo

Review Cycle Annual or upon major business, security, compliance, or system change

1. Purpose

This policy establishes financial governance requirements for cloud resources used by Northstar Digital Services,
Inc.. It supports cost visibility, budget accountability, tagging, rightsizing, forecasting, and timely remediation of
waste.

2. Scope

• Applies to all cloud accounts, subscriptions, projects, tenants, sandboxes, and production environments.

• Applies to compute, storage, networking, AI/ML, database, monitoring, backup, and third-party marketplace
services.

• Applies to employees, contractors, vendors, and managed service providers who provision or manage cloud
services.

3. Cost Ownership

Cost Area Owner Expectation

Application workloads Application owner Forecast monthly spend and approve scaling
changes.

Shared platforms Platform engineering Allocate costs using tags, chargeback, or showback
reporting.

Security tooling Security engineering Budget recurring controls and monitor log ingestion
growth.

AI/ML services AI platform owner Track model usage, token consumption, endpoint
utilization, and storage.



Northstar Digital Services, Inc. | Internal Use Only Page 2

4. Required Tags

Tag Example Required For

cost-center FIN-204 All resources

application policy-assistant All application resources

environment dev, test, stage, prod All resources

owner team-email or service
owner

All resources

data-classification public, internal,
confidential, restricted

Storage, databases, AI knowledge bases

expiration-date 2026-03-31 Temporary environments and experiments

5. Budget and Alert Rules

• Each production workload must have an approved monthly budget.

• Alerts must be configured at 50%, 80%, 90%, and 100% of forecasted monthly spend.

• Any single-day spend increase above 25% must be reviewed by the owning team within one business day.

• AI/ML experiments must have usage limits or quotas before being opened to multiple users.

6. Provisioning Standards

• Infrastructure should be provisioned through approved Infrastructure as Code pipelines.

• Default instance sizes, storage classes, and retention settings must be reviewed during design.

• Non-production resources should use scheduling, auto-stop, or deletion policies where technically feasible.

• Public network egress, high-volume logs, and managed AI endpoints must be cost-reviewed before
production launch.

7. Optimization Requirements

1 Review idle compute, orphaned storage, unattached disks, snapshots, and unused public IP addresses
monthly.

2 Use reserved capacity, savings plans, or committed-use discounts only after workload stability is validated.

3 Archive or delete logs and backups according to retention policy.

4 Rightsize databases, container clusters, and search/vector indexes based on measured utilization.

8. Exceptions and Enforcement

Resources missing required tags may be quarantined, stopped, or escalated to management. Emergency
exceptions are allowed for incident response but must be corrected within five business days.

Document ID: PROC-IT-110 | Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: 2026-01-01 | Classification: Internal

Field Value

Company Northstar Digital Services, Inc.

Document Owner IT Service Management

Audience Employees, contractors, managers, IT support, security, and finance teams

Purpose Sample enterprise content for a Retrieval-Augmented Generation demo

Review Cycle Annual or upon major business, security, compliance, or system change

1. Purpose

This document defines the standard incident management process for Northstar Digital Services, Inc.. It provides
a consistent approach to detecting, triaging, resolving, communicating, and learning from technology incidents.

2. Scope

• Applies to incidents affecting production services, internal business applications, cloud platforms, data
pipelines, security controls, and customer-facing systems.

• Applies to incidents reported by monitoring tools, users, customers, vendors, or employees.

• Does not replace the Information Security Incident Response Plan for confirmed cybersecurity breaches, but
the two processes may run in parallel.

3. Severity Levels

Severity Definition Target
Response

Example

SEV-1
Critical

Major outage, data exposure,
safety impact, or
executive-level business
disruption.

15 minutes Production authentication
unavailable for all users.

SEV-2 High Significant degradation or
outage affecting many users or
a critical business process.

30 minutes Policy Assistant search is
unavailable for the compliance
team.

SEV-3
Medium

Partial impact with workaround
available.

4 business hours One integration is delayed but
manual processing is available.



Northstar Digital Services, Inc. | Internal Use Only Page 2

Severity Definition Target
Response

Example

SEV-4 Low Minor issue, informational alert,
or service request misclassified
as incident.

1 business day Single user cannot access a
non-critical application.

4. Incident Lifecycle

1 Detect and report the issue through monitoring, support ticket, chat escalation, or phone bridge.

2 Triage the symptoms, affected services, user impact, and potential business impact.

3 Assign severity, incident commander, technical lead, communications lead, and scribe when needed.

4 Mitigate customer or business impact as quickly and safely as possible.

5 Resolve root cause or implement a durable workaround.

6 Validate service recovery with monitoring, smoke tests, and business owner confirmation.

7 Close the incident after documentation and required communications are complete.

5. Communication Requirements

• SEV-1 updates must be sent every 30 minutes until stable, then hourly until closure.

• SEV-2 updates must be sent at least hourly during active impact.

• Customer-facing impacts require approved external messaging through the communications lead.

• Incident notes must include timeline, decisions, commands executed, changes made, and validation
evidence.

6. Post-Incident Review

A post-incident review is required for all SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents within five business days. The review must
identify contributing factors, customer impact, detection gaps, action items, owners, and due dates. The review is
blameless and focused on improving systems and processes.

7. Change Freeze and Emergency Change

During active SEV-1 or SEV-2 incidents, non-essential production changes to affected services are paused.
Emergency changes must be approved by the incident commander and documented in the incident record.

8. Metrics

• Mean Time to Detect (MTTD)

• Mean Time to Acknowledge (MTTA)

• Mean Time to Restore (MTTR)

• Incident recurrence rate

• Post-incident action item completion rate
